text: The most difficult aspect of improving my speaking is how to manage anxiety in timed oral exams. In high-stakes speaking tests it is a normal problem that candidates freeze under pressure. When I was doing my mock IELTS speaking, for example, I always spent most of my time hesitating before answering part two. I switched my strategies after that mock so I seldom freeze in the same way. I completed three timed speaking drills each week and I always recorded myself first so I can push myself to answer faster.

text: A general principle of exam reading is that you will not finish every item if you linger. I realized I need a clearer concept of priority because last season I learned nothing from random practice. When I spent two hours on one passage I always left the last questions blank. Next time I will improve by leaving hard items and returning later. I feel more confident when I reflect on timing after each mock.

text: When I preparing for Gaokao, I feel very boring, my English is not good, and I decide to study hard for it. But there are so many tasks about math, Chinese, chemistry and physical, so ignore the English study for a long time. I don't write the English homework, and i often write all the subjects homework when i listen to my English teacher talks some important knowledges, so my English become bad and my English teacher was often critical to class because of the bad scores we had. When I only have two weeks to prepare Gaokao, I feel afraid because my English is so bad. I want to study English immediately, but it's too late. So when I write the English test in Gaokao, I feel regret. I want to improve my English in university.
